subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 55 years old, male. I've been having some right shoulder pain for a few weeks now. It started after doing some work in my backyard on a bunch of different projects, and it just hasn't gone away. It's been really sore, especially on the outside of my shoulder, and it hurts when I move it. Doctor: Could you describe the nature of the pain (e.g., sharp, dull, burning) and whether it radiates to other areas? Have you experienced any swelling, redness, or limited range of motion in the shoulder? Have you had any prior shoulder injuries or surgeries? Patient: The pain is more of a soreness, kinda like a dull ache, and it's mostly on the outside of my shoulder. It doesn't really radiate anywhere else, but it definitely hurts when I move it, especially when I raise my arm. I have had some issues with that same shoulder before from playing baseball when I was younger, but nothing major. I don't remember any surgeries on it. Doctor: Have you undergone any imaging studies or consultations for this shoulder pain, and if so, what were the findings or recommendations? Patient: No, I haven't had any imaging studies done for this yet, but my doctor mentioned looking at an X-ray and there was no fracture. They did say they might order an MRI since I've had some issues before. I'm not sure what exactly they're looking for, but I'm hoping it's nothing too serious. Patient: No, I haven't experienced any weakness, numbness, or tingling in my right arm or hand.
